title: Great books and their ideas
description: Who wrote the books people keep returning to, and the main idea of each.

ideas.title: Epics and journeys
ideas.summary: The oldest great stories follow a hero through war, wandering or the afterlife toward home or understanding.

items.q: To which poet are the Iliad and the Odyssey traditionally attributed?
What is the story of Homer's Odyssey?
items.a: Odysseus's ten-year journey home to Ithaca after the Trojan War

items.q: Which Roman poet wrote the Aeneid, the epic of a Trojan refugee whose descendants found Rome?
Who wrote the Divine Comedy, and what are its three parts?

ideas.title: Philosophy and the good life
ideas.summary: Ancient philosophers asked what justice and happiness are, and answered that the good life is a life of virtue.

items.q: Which dialogue by Plato asks what justice is and imagines an ideal city ruled by philosophers?
In Plato's allegory of the cave, what do the shadows on the wall represent?
items.a: The appearances that people mistake for reality

items.q: In the Nicomachean Ethics, how does Aristotle describe a virtue such as courage?
items.a: As a mean between two extremes, one of excess and one of deficiency

items.q: Which Roman emperor wrote the Meditations, a private notebook of Stoic philosophy?

ideas.title: Power and the state
ideas.summary: Modern political thought asks how power is really won and kept, and what makes a government legitimate.

items.q: Who wrote The Prince, and what is its central lesson for rulers?
items.a: Machiavelli; a ruler must do what keeps the state secure, even when it is not conventionally moral

items.q: Which 1651 book by Thomas Hobbes argues that people need a strong sovereign to escape a war of all against all?
Which English philosopher's Second Treatise of Government argued that government rests on the consent of the governed?
Which 1748 work by Montesquieu argued for separating legislative, executive and judicial power?

ideas.title: Shakespeare's tragedies
ideas.summary: Shakespeare's great tragedies follow powerful people undone by doubt, ambition, jealousy and pride.

items.q: Which Shakespeare play contains the line "To be, or not to be, that is the question"?
In Shakespeare's Macbeth, what drives Macbeth to murder King Duncan?
items.a: Ambition, stirred by the witches' prophecy and by Lady Macbeth

items.q: Which Shakespeare tragedy turns on a general's jealousy, inflamed by the villain Iago?
Which Shakespeare tragedy begins with an old king dividing his kingdom among his daughters?

ideas.title: The novel
ideas.summary: The novel follows inner lives at length, testing a character's ideals and illusions against the world.

items.q: Who wrote Don Quixote, often called the first modern novel?
Who wrote Pride and Prejudice, published in 1813?
Which Dostoevsky novel follows Raskolnikov, a student who commits murder and is undone by his conscience?
Which novel by Herman Melville tells of Captain Ahab's obsessive hunt for a white whale?

ideas.title: Science and the modern mind
ideas.summary: A few books changed the picture of nature: the Earth moves, one set of laws governs motion, and species evolve.

items.q: Which astronomer's 1543 book On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres argued that the Earth orbits the Sun?
Which 1687 book by Isaac Newton set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation?
items.a: The Principia (Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy)

items.q: Who wrote On the Origin of Species, and in what year was it published?
What is the central idea of Darwin's On the Origin of Species?
items.a: Species evolve by natural selection: traits that aid survival and reproduction spread
